judgment_text:
Common Prayer: This criminal revision petition has been filed under Section 438 r/w 442 of BNSS Act to set aside the judgment dated 9-9-2025 in Criminal Appeal Nos. 271 and 272 of 2022 on the file of the VI Additional Sessions Court, Chennai thereby confirming the conviction of the petitioners by judgment dated 29-9-2022 in C.C. Nos. 1800 and 3653 and 2020 on the file of the Metropolitan Magistrate-Fast Track Court No. 1, Allikulam, Egmore, Chennai for an alleged offence under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act and sentencing the petitioner to undergo simple imprisonment for two years and to pay double the cheque amount of compensation to the respondent within one month in default the petitioner to undergo six months simple and consequently acquit the petitioner/accused of the alleged offence

COMMON ORDER

The petitioner has preferred the above revision challenging the judgment passed by the VI Additional Sessions Court, Chennai, in Criminal Appeal Nos. 271 and 272 of 2022 dated 9-9-2025, confirming the judgment of the learned judicial Metropolitan Magistrate-Fast Track Court No. 1, Allikulam, Egmore, Chennai, in C.C. Nos. 1800 and 3653 and 2020 dated 29-9-2022 convicting the petitioner for the offence under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act and sentenced him to undergo two years simple imprisonment and to pay double the cheque amount within one month in default, to undergo six months Simple Imprisonment.

2. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner and the learned counsel for the respondents and perused the materials available on record.

3. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that in pursuance of the direction of this Court, the matter was referred to mediation centre and a settlement agreement was also entered on 16-2-2026.

4. The settlement agreement filed by the parties dated 16-2-2026 is extracted hereunder:

IN THE HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT MADRAS

(Criminal Jurisdiction)

Crl.R.C. No. 2238 & 2239 Of 2025

Cannane S/o Mr Irissappane, No. 98, West Street, Gandhi Thiru Nallur, Puducherry-605009 … Petitioner;

-Vs—

1. R. Manoharan, S/o. Ramalingam (Died),

2. Jamuna, W/o. Late R. Manoharan

3. M. Mohana Priya, D/o. Late R. Manoharan

4. M. Tharika, D/o. Late R. Manoharan

All are residing at No. 92/7, 8th Block, North Avenue Road, Muthamizh Nagar, Kodungaiyur, Chennai - 600118 … Respondents.

SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT

This settlement agreement entered into on this the 13-2-2026 between

Whereas

1. Disputes and differences had arisen between the parties hereto and a Criminal Revision in Crl.RC Nos. 2238 and 2239 of 2025 came to be filed challenging the judgment dated 9-9-2025 passed in Crl.A. No. 271 & 272 of 2022 by the The learned VI Additional Sessions Judge, Chennai.

2. The matter was referred to mediation vide order dated 19-1-2026 passed by the Hon'ble High Court, Madras.

3. The parties agreed that Mrs V. Malleeswari and Mr A. Palaniappan would act as their Mediator.

4. Several meetings were held during the process of mediation from 29-1-2026 to 13-2-2026 and the parties have with assistance of the mediator voluntarily arrived to an amicable solution resolving the above-mentioned disputes and differences.

5. The parties hereto confirm and declare that they have voluntarily and of their own free will arrived at this Settlement agreement in the presence of the Mediator.

6. The following settlement has been arrived at between the parties hereto:

(a) in full and final settlement of all claims arising out of the subject matter of Crl.R.C. Nos. 2238 & 2239 of 2025, the Petitioner has agreed to pay a total sum of Rs 4,00,000 (Rupees Four Lakhs only) to the Respondents.

(b) Out of the said total settlement amount of Rs 4,00,000, the Petitioner has already deposited a sum of Rs 40,000 (Rupees Forty Thousand only) in C.C. No. 1800 of 2020 on the file of FTC-I, Metropolitan Magistrate Court, Egmore, Chennai and a sum of Rs 92,000 (Rupees Ninety Two Thousand only) in C.C No. 3653 of 2022 on the file of FTC-I Metropolitan Magistrate Court, Egmore, Chennai in pursuance to the conditional order dated 22-12-2022 passed in Crl.A. Nos. 271 & 272 of 2022 on the file of the The learned VI Additional Sessions Judge, Chennai.

(c) Further, a sum of Rs 50,000 (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) has been deposited by the Petitioner in C.C. No. 3653 of 2022 on the file of FTC-I Metropolitan Magistrate Court, Egmore, Chennai in compliance with the order dated 4-11-2025 passed by this Hon'ble Court in Crl.R.C. Nos. 2238 of 2025.

(d) Thus, a total sum of Rs 1,82,000 (Rupees One Lakh Eighty Two Thousand only) already stands deposited to the credit of the above cases, which shall be appropriated by the Respondents towards the settlement amount.

(e) The Petitioner hereby conveys his no objection for the Respondents to withdraw the said deposited total amount of Rs 1,82,000 and the original deposit receipts bearing SI. Nos. 03993 & 03994 dated 29-12-2022 and No. 09627 dated 11-12-2025 have been handed over by the Petitioner to the Respondents on the date of this Settlement agreement:

(f) The Petitioner has today i.e. 13-2-2026, paid a further sum of Rs 68,000 (Rupees Sixty-Eight Thousand only) to the Respondents by way of cash, which the Respondents hereby acknowledge having received to their full satisfaction.

(g) The remaining balance amount of Rs 1,50,000 (Rupees One Lakh Fifty only) shall be paid by the Petitioner to the Respondents on or before 13-3-2026.

(h) Upon receipt of the entire settlement amount of Rs 4,00,000, the Respondents agree that they shall have no further claims, demands or grievances of any nature whatsoever against the Petitioner arising out of the subject matter of the above Criminal Revision Cases.

(i) The parties further agree that this Settlement agreement may be taken on record by this Hon'ble Court and that appropriate orders may be passed in Crl.R.C. Nos. 2238 & 2239 of 2025 in terms of this settlement.

7. By signing this agreement the parties hereto state that they have no further claims or demands against each other with respect to Crl.R.C. Nos. 2238 & 2239 of 2025 and all disputes and differences in this regard have been amicably settled by the parties hereto through the process of Mediation.

Date:— 16-2-2026

Parties' Signature:

5. In view of the above factual position, it is amply clear that both of them have compromised the issue. Therefore, this Court permits the parties to compound the offence Accordingly, the petitioner is acquitted and the judgment of the VI Additional Sessions Court, Chennai, in Criminal Appeal Nos. 271 and 272 of 2022 dated 9-9-2025, confirming the judgment of conviction and sentence dated 29-9-2022 passed by the learned Metropolitan Magistrate-Fast Track Court No. 1, Allikulam, Egmore, in C.C. Nos. 1800 and 3653 and 2020, is hereby set aside. As a consequence the conviction and sentence passed against the petitioner in C.C. Nos. 1800 and 3653 and 2020 is also set aside. Accordingly, the Criminal Revision Cases are allowed in terms of the above compromise. The fine amount, if any, paid by the petitioner shall be refunded. The bail bond, if any, executed shall stand discharged.
